content:
marta: Quick check — I'm running a dry-run for lateral-move detection on the private deployment. We need a quick RBAC tweak so the monitoring SA can tail audit logs, plus a way to push signed, KMS-encrypted audit bundles to our on-prem SIEM. Any blockers?

liam: +1 for the detection rules. What RBAC changes did you have in mind?

marta: Right now the monitoring SA (monitoring-agent@priv-project) only has read on /var/log/audit. I want to add a very narrow role: allow get/list/watch on ConfigMaps/Secrets in the telemetry ns for leader-election + ability to read the audit socket. Not broad cluster-admin. Example role draft below.

raj: share the draft pls — we should enforce resourceNames where possible. Also consider a PodSecurityPolicy / PSP-ish constraint for the SA so it can't exec into other pods.

marta: Copying draft role:
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  namespace: telemetry
  name: monitoring-audit-tail
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods/log", "pods/exec"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["configmaps", "secrets"]
  verbs: ["get", "list"]
  resourceNames: ["telemetry-leader", "telemetry-config"]
```
Notes: deny pods/exec in PSP for the SA; the Role allows only log fetches.

olivia: Don't allow pods/exec at all for that SA. Also, we must ensure audit logs are immutable after collection — signed via KMS/HSM before writing to long-term store. Is the plan to encrypt in-transit and at-rest using our onprem HSM?

marta: Yes, plan is: monitoring agent collects logs -> signs and encrypts with local HSM (Vault Transit or HSM wrap) -> writes to append-only NFS/MinIO bucket -> SIEM pulls or we push via signed bundles. We want cryptographic attestations so we can prove tamper-evidence.

devon: For the encryption step, we should standardize on Vault transit with HSM-backed keys for now. Example encrypt flow: `vault write transit/encrypt/telem plaintext=$(base64 < bundle.tar)` then push the ciphertext. Keep the plaintext never on disk.

liam: How do we handle key rotation without losing the ability to verify old bundles? Need versioning metadata in the bundle header.

marta: Exactly — include key_version, key_id, and a detached signature. We store signed manifest.json next to the ciphertext. That manifest should contain file hashes, signer key id, timestamp, and vault key_version.

raj: On network policy side — I propose a default-deny NS policy for the telemetry namespace and explicit egress to: SIEM collector IPs, HSM/Vault cluster, and KMS-proxy. Also restrict DNS to internal resolver only. Quick example:
```yaml
kind: NetworkPolicy
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: telemetry-egress-tight
  namespace: telemetry
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.20.0/24   # vault/hsm
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.30.0/32   # siem-collector
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8200  # vault
```
This prevents lateral egress to app namespaces.

olivia: Make sure that NetworkPolicy is enforced by the CNI — we use Calico in priv deployments, so fine. Also audit CNI logs for rule drops.

devon: For detection rules, we should pipeline a minimal set of heuristics to flag lateral activity:
- monitoring agent observes pod-to-pod traffic to non-whitelisted ports
- unexpected use of service account tokens from app namespaces
- sudden spikes in API server read activity from a single SA

marta: Can we get the API-server audit webhook to include the agent's request-id so we can trace back?

liam: We can add a custom field in the audit annotation when the agent forwards bundles, but the initial audit entries are generated by kube-apiserver. Use the audit webhook to copy the requestUID into the bundle manifest.

sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-334 — "Priv-deploy lateral-move-detection dry-run" assigned to @marta, severity: P3.

olivia: For incident response — runbook proposal:
1) If lateral detected -> isolate offending pod by applying an EmergencyNetworkPolicy that blocks all egress/ingress except kube-dns and logging collector.
2) Snapshot pod filesystem and collect mounted secrets metadata.
3) Revoke affected SA tokens (rotate secrets) and create ephemeral replacement SAs.
4) Push encrypted evidence bundle to secure archive and open investigation ticket.

raj: Agree. Make sure the EmergencyNetworkPolicy is pre-created and stored in gitops, referenced by name so we can `kubectl apply -f emergency-egress-block.yaml` quickly. Also pre-stage a kubelet certificate to allow for forensic pulls if node becomes unreachable.

marta: I'll add the following action items:
- PR for Role/RoleBinding + PSP-deny for exec (owner: @liam)
- NetworkPolicy PR for telemetry ns + emergency policy (owner: @raj)
- Vault transit integration doc + manifest schema (owner: @devon)
- Runbook edits for isolation and evidence handling (owner: @olivia)
- Test plan: simulate lateral move using a controlled pod, verify detection + IR (owner: @marta)

liam: I'll open the PR today for the RBAC change. Quick ask: include an acceptance test that tries `kubectl exec` with the monitoring SA and expects 403.

olivia: Also include a retention and WORM policy note for the archive. We should be able to audit-read only via a separate read-only auditor SA.

devon: I'll draft the Vault transit playbook and the encryption headers. Propose manifest fields: [bundle_id, signer_kid, key_version, request_uid, sha256_sum, timestamp].

marta: Awesome. If nobody objects, I'll run the dry-run tomorrow night in staging and post results here. :thumbsup:

liam: No objections from me.

olivia: SGTM.

sec-bot: Reminder scheduled: Dry-run checklist reminder in #eng-oncall in 12 hours.

marta: Thanks everyone — I'll update the thread with PR links and test output after the run.
